title: Build and Manage Containers
objective: Use Ansible to build images, manage multi-container applications, and configure containers as inventory targets.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.note: Original synthesis of the chapter's Flask, data, MySQL, and Hubot container examples.

paragraphs: Containers package processes and dependencies into images, then run them with isolated filesystems and networking. Persistent data belongs in managed volumes rather than the writable container layer.

Ansible can build images and manage networks, volumes, and containers through collection modules. A multi-container application separates concerns—for example, application and database services—while variables define images, ports, and credentials.

With ansible_connection set to docker, a running container can become a managed inventory target. This is useful for image construction experiments, though modern image pipelines should minimize mutable post-build configuration.
explanation.rule: Treat images as immutable releases and keep persistent state outside disposable containers.

examples.title: Container Intent
examples.code:
container:
  name: web
  image: example/flask:1.0
  state: started
  restart_policy: unless-stopped
examples.note: Pin an image release rather than relying on latest.

checks.question: Where should persistent database data live?
options: Only in the container writable layer

feedback.incorrect: Containers are disposable; persistent data needs external storage.

assignment.title: Define a Stable Web Container
assignment.brief: Describe a started web container using example/flask:1.0 with unless-stopped restart policy.
requirements: Set name, pinned image, state, and restart policy.
assignment.solutionCode:

  name: web
  image: example/flask:1.0
